items.label: f09-practice-ladder
items.front: 05-PRACTICE: how do the checks run, and what are the seven exercises?
items.back: Each check is a dependency-free node --test file that compiles src/ and test/ into a fresh temp directory and never touches data/expenses.txt. Exercises: 1 a Save now menu option that reports the real outcome; 2 plain decimals only; 3 an exit-code contract; 4 a durable id allocation; 5 a human message for a bad id; 6 a deterministic page ordered by date then id; 7 optimistic concurrency in the manager.

items.label: f07-port-schema
items.front: The Express sketch: how is the expenses table declared, and which pieces make up its request validation?
items.back: Table: integer id, title, amount_cents with CHECK (amount_cents > 0), category, date, note defaulting to '' and version defaulting to 1. Validation: a money schema that turns text into integer cents and requires a positive value, a day schema that requires a real calendar day, and a body object with trimmed, length-bounded title and category and a note of at most 500 characters. express.json is limited to 16kb.

items.label: f05-coverage-map
items.front: The 23 expense-tracker tests: which failure boundaries does each group cover?
items.back: Domain: precision and category normalization. Manager: identity, invalid-update preservation, copy isolation, exhaustion and deletion. Storage, with real temporary files: empty fields, escapes, corruption, duplicate IDs, repeated replacement and failed moves. One end-to-end Java case updates and deletes records, saves, builds a new manager and inspects the restored state.

items.label: f06-inspect-the-file
items.front: A save/reload or update test fails. How does the lesson tell you to investigate before changing the manager?
items.back: Inspect the physical file first: Get-Content -LiteralPath on the data file, replacing each tab with a visible <TAB> marker. Put breakpoints in load, parseLine and splitPreservingEscapes, and in App.loadExpenses to see whether a load error reaches the menu or the save. For updates, break before new Expense and before expenses.set, and hold a reference to the old immutable expense to confirm its fields never change.

items.label: f10-without-powershell
items.front: How do you compile and run the expense tracker's regression tests without PowerShell?
items.back: javac --release 17 -Xlint:all -d out $(find src test -name '*.java'), then java -cp out expensetracker.RegressionTests.

items.label: f03-atomic-is-not-everything
items.front: save() writes a temp file and moves it over the target with ATOMIC_MOVE. Name three guarantees this does NOT give.
items.back: No cross-process lock (two app instances can overwrite each other), no compare-and-swap version check on the user's edit, and no guaranteed survival of a power loss (the temp file is never forced to disk).

items.label: f01-validate-in-constructor
items.front: Why does the Expense constructor enforce the invariants (positive id, nonblank title and category, two-place positive amount) instead of only the menu code?
items.back: Records enter from two places: the menu and the saved file. Validating only menu input would leave the file-loading path unprotected, so the rule lives where every Expense is built.

items.label: f04-normalize-fields-not-lines
items.front: What general parsing lesson does the empty-note fix teach?
items.back: Normalization that is fine for recognizing a blank line can destroy structured data. Normalize individual fields by their own contract, not the whole record (in a web app: trimming a signed payload, or turning an empty field into a missing one).

items.label: f02-dual-write
items.front: What is a dual write, and what is the fix the course gives for it?
items.back: One logical change that needs two separate durable writes (for example rows in one file and a next-id counter in another). They can fail independently. The fix is to make it one write: same file under one atomic move, or one database transaction.

items.label: f08-mapping-and-exercise
items.front: Express port: how does 'build the replacement first' map, and what does the exercise ask for?
items.back: Building a valid replacement first becomes safeParse before the UPDATE, so a validation failure touches nothing. Exercise (in a separate project): four tests covering an invalid amount, an unknown id, a stale version and a good update, then load data/expenses.txt with one script and prove the escaped-tab note round-trips.
